name: Naproxen
reviewed_by: William Gregory M. Rivero, MD, FPCP, DPSN
drafted_by: AI-assisted draft (Claude) for review by Dr. W. Rivero
summary: Naproxen is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) excreted mainly in urine as conjugates, which can accumulate in kidney failure. The US label does not recommend naproxen-containing products at creatinine clearance (CrCl) below 30 mL/min. NSAID kidney risks (acute kidney injury, hyperkalemia, fluid retention) apply at any level of kidney function.

bands.recommendation: Usual: naproxen 250 to 500 mg twice daily, or naproxen sodium 275 to 550 mg twice daily; lowest effective dose, shortest duration (label).

No label dose change at CrCl ≥30. Monitor creatinine, potassium and blood pressure; avoid volume depletion and the ACE inhibitor or ARB plus diuretic combination (label 5.6). Acute gout in CKD: low-dose colchicine or glucocorticoids are preferred over NSAIDs (KDIGO 2024 PP 3.14.3).
bands.short: No dose change; monitor SCr, K, BP

bands.recommendation: Not recommended at CrCl <30 mL/min (moderate to severe and severe impairment; label 8.7). Naproxen metabolites accumulate in kidney failure. Acute gout in CKD: low-dose colchicine or glucocorticoids are preferred over NSAIDs (KDIGO 2024 PP 3.14.3).

Not recommended at CrCl <30 mL/min (moderate to severe and severe impairment; label 8.7). Naproxen metabolites accumulate in kidney failure. Acute gout in CKD: low-dose colchicine or glucocorticoids are preferred over NSAIDs (KDIGO 2024 PP 3.14.3).

hd.text: Not recommended (CrCl <30; label). NSAIDs may hasten loss of residual kidney function.

pd.text: Not recommended (CrCl <30; label). NSAIDs may hasten loss of residual kidney function.

crrt.text: Avoid: NSAIDs can worsen acute kidney injury.

dialyzable: Unlikely: hemodialysis may not be useful because of high protein binding (over 99%; label 10).
monitoring: Creatinine, potassium and blood pressure in CKD, heart failure, liver disease, dehydration or with ACE inhibitors, ARBs or diuretics. Naproxen sodium contains sodium (about 2 mEq per 500 mg naproxen).

pediatric.approved_ages: Juvenile arthritis (label; suspension preferred for weight-based dosing). Tablets not appropriate under 50 kg.
pediatric.max_dose: Not stated separately; adult maximum applies.

renal.recommendation: No pediatric kidney data; at CrCl ≥30 the label gives no dose change. Monitor creatinine and potassium.
renal.short: No dose data; monitor SCr, K

renal.recommendation: Not recommended at CrCl <30 (label statement not limited by age).
